summary:
SPHEREx Explorer is an interactive six-page astrophysics web platform developed for the 2026 NASA Space Apps Challenge. It transforms complex NASA/IPAC SPHEREx infrared survey data into an accessible environment for exploring the universe, analysing celestial objects, and investigating potential discoveries.

The platform features an interactive Sky Explorer for inspecting infrared images and FITS data, a Time Machine for comparing observations across different epochs, a Discoveries database for examining confirmed objects and unconfirmed candidates, and a Spectra viewer for analysing 102 near-infrared spectral channels. It also integrates cross-mission information from Gaia, WISE, SPLICES, and NEOSSat, alongside COSMIC AI, an astrophysics assistant that explains scientific observations.

By combining data visualisation, multi-epoch analysis, spectral exploration, and AI-assisted explanations, SPHEREx Explorer helps address the challenge of making massive SPHEREx datasets easier to understand and investigate. It encourages scientific curiosity, supports the identification of unusual astronomical phenomena, and makes advanced astrophysics more accessible to students, researchers, and space enthusiasts.
details:
SPHEREx Explorer is an interactive astrophysics platform designed to transform complex infrared astronomical data into an engaging and understandable exploration experience. It consists of six interconnected sections: Home, Sky Explorer, Time Machine, Discoveries, Spectra, and Mission & Data.

The Sky Explorer allows users to inspect celestial fields using RA/Dec coordinates, different FITS image layers, spectral bands, detectors, and visualisation controls. The Time Machine compares multiple observation epochs through image subtraction, overlays, blinking, and time-lapse playback to highlight the movement and variability of celestial objects. The Discoveries section presents confirmed astronomical targets separately from algorithmic candidates, while the Spectra section visualises 102 near-infrared channels and important molecular absorption features. COSMIC AI provides context-aware astrophysics explanations through Google's Gemini API, with a built-in scientific fallback system.

The platform uses cross-mission information from SPHEREx, Gaia, WISE, SPLICES, and NEOSSat to demonstrate how different astronomical datasets complement one another. Its FITS service supports parsing and generating FITS files, including WCS metadata and SPHEREx-related HDU layers.

Technologies Used: We developed the platform using React 19, TypeScript, Vite, Tailwind CSS, HTML, and CSS. We used Recharts for spectral visualisation, HTML Canvas for interactive infrared-style imagery, Express.js and Node.js for the backend, and Google's Gemini API for COSMIC AI. Astronomy calculations, coordinate conversions, and FITS processing are handled through custom TypeScript services.

Our creative approach was to combine an interactive astronomical observatory, a multi-epoch analysis laboratory, a spectral explorer, and an AI research assistant into one platform. We considered scientific accuracy, usability, accessibility, responsive design, data interpretation, and the importance of clearly distinguishing confirmed discoveries from unverified candidates.

Our intended impact is to make advanced astrophysics more accessible, encourage students and space enthusiasts to investigate astronomical phenomena, and demonstrate how SPHEREx's infrared observations can support the exploration of moving objects, brown dwarfs, variable stars, and possible outer Solar System candidates.
